key_insight: EEG-Xplain provides a unified, multi-dimensional attribution framework to make EEG foundation models interpretable across spatial, temporal, and frequency domains.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps engineers and clinicians validate black-box EEG models by turning internal model signals into reliable, human-readable explanations for deployment and debugging.
method: Uses gradient-, perturbation-, and activation-based attribution methods across different EEG architectures.
Maps critical channels, salient time segments, and frequency-rhythm contributions using topographic maps, heatmaps, and spectral perturbations.
Adds population-level reliability checks with AOPC and cross-method consistency, then converts outputs into LLM-generated natural language reports.
evidence_signal: Experiments on Mumtaz2016 and TUAB show explanations aligned with known neurophysiological markers while also revealing possible artifact and spurious-pattern dependence.
watch_item: Explanation quality depends on perturbation choices and model behavior, so artifacts or unstable attribution methods may still produce misleading interpretations.
paper_title: EEG-Xplain: Decoding Neural Black-Boxes of EEG Foundation Models
